title: Emrys and the Safehouse
premise: Oscar Sandoval, a whistle-blower living under four names, has built a career on cases no one wants attributed—until a dead man's voiceprint unlocks a server in Lisbon and drags her into a plot to destroy a ferry terminal in an 'accident' engineered by the very agency that once protected her. Racing across three countries with Emrys, the paranoid architect of the safehouse network who trusts no one, least of all her, she discovers the attack is bait designed to flush out every ghost like herself. To stop it, Oscar must choose between erasing her identities forever and using them as weapons, sacrificing the anonymity that kept her alive. In the end she lets one name die publicly, saves hundreds, and walks away under a fifth name—finally her own.
about_author: Gideon Lockridge is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing security briefings before turning to fiction. He lives off-grid in coastal Maine and refuses interviews, insisting his biography should be shorter than his characters' rap sheets.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Living as 'Mara Voss' in Rotterdam, she finishes a quiet job exposing a shipping fraud and burns the identity per protocol. The beat: disciplined loneliness—the cost of being no one, and the strange comfort of it.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A dead contact's voice recording arrives with coordinates and a passphrase; when she speaks it aloud, a server in Lisbon unlocks and streams files naming her first alias. Beat: dread—the past has a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In a converted chapel safehouse outside Porto, he detects the breach he built the network to prevent and prepares to hunt the intruder. Beat: cold fury curdling into curiosity—he recognizes the passphrase's origin.

chapters.title: Chapel of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar reaches the Lisbon drop point and finds not data but a summons; Emrys intercepts her there, gun drawn, demanding to know how she has Halvorsen's voiceprint. Beat: mutual recognition of two people built for hiding.

chapters.title: Terms of Shelter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Uneasy truce at the chapel: he shows her the server contents—a staged-accident attack plan targeting the Calais ferry terminal, signed with the internal codename of the agency that once employed them both. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What Halvorsen Knew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She reconstructs Halvorsen's final months through cached files: he found the plan, tried to warn the network, and died in a fall ruled accidental. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose—this is justice outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Bait Hypothesis
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He argues the attack may be theater designed to lure exposed assets into the open; Oscar counters that believing him means doing nothing while people die. Beat: ideological fracture inside the fragile partnership.

chapters.title: Bruges Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using her second name, 'Ines,' she meets a retired analyst who confirms the operation is real but insists the target list includes the safehouse network itself. Beat: paranoia vindicated—the walls are already mapped.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They find their Brussels node burned, its keeper missing; Emrys executes emergency protocol, scattering evidence and burning years of careful work. Beat: loss—an archivist watching his life's archive turn to ash.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Deep in the stolen files she finds the mechanism: a maintenance drone swarm timed to a fuel transfer, deniable, precise, scheduled in nine days. Beat: cold clarity—the accident has a clock.

chapters.title: Someone From Before
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A man from her first life, Deputy Director Corliss, contacts her through her sister, offering immunity for silence. Beat: temptation and rage—the law she once believed in is the thing selling the lie.

chapters.title: Sister
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She risks everything to see Elena in Antwerp, lying about who she is now, unable to say goodbye properly. Beat: heartbreak—inheritance of fear passed down a family line; identity as something you owe others.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He reveals the network's last unburned asset: a clean identity never issued, held in reserve for whoever survives. Beat: quiet tenderness disguised as procedure—he intends it for her.

chapters.title: Calais Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Posing as port contractors, they map the terminal and confirm the drone staging site, but Emrys trips a sensor and they barely exfiltrate. Beat: adrenaline and trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Corliss's Offer, Revised
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corliss escalates: cooperate or the agency detonates the plot early and pins it on 'Mara Voss.' Beat: trap closing—her names are being weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Turning the Key
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He proposes the unthinkable: broadcast the entire file trove publicly, torching every identity including theirs, forcing exposure over secrecy. Beat: conviction—justice that requires self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Vote of Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar hesitates—public burn means Elena becomes a target too—then finds proof Corliss plans to kill the whistleblowers regardless. She agrees. Beat: resolve; the decision that defines the book.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Attack day: they infiltrate the control shack, spoof the drone swarm's geofence toward open water, and trigger the public dump simultaneously. Beat: white-knuckle climax, every skill earned across 21 chapters deployed at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The leak detonates globally; Corliss is arrested by his own agency's internal affairs; the 'accident' becomes the biggest story of the year. Beat: vertiginous vindication—justice arriving loud after years of whispering.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He surveys the ashes of his network and, instead of rebuilding it, hands Oscar the fifth-name dossier and the only physical key. Beat: release—the inheritor named at last.

chapters.title: Elena's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Under her real name—her actual, original name—she sits across from her sister and tells the truth, all of it, for the first time. Beat: catharsis; identity reclaimed not as cover but as gift.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Keeps Its Silence
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Months later, a new voiceprint arrives at a fresh address; Oscar and Emrys exchange a look over the encrypted terminal. Beat: quiet continuation—some inheritances you don't get to refuse.
